title: The prayer said every day
translation: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship; You alone we ask for help. Guide us on the straight path: of those You blessed, not those under anger, nor those astray.
body: **Al-Raḥmān** is older than the Qur'an: inscriptions from **Himyar in Yemen** call the one God Raḥmānān from the 5th century, first in Jewish, later in Christian texts. Like the **Lord's Prayer**, which Luther's Small Catechism explains line by line, the Fatiha is prayed daily and moves from praising God to asking: guide us.
question: Both prayers praise God before asking for anything. Why might that order matter?
